destinations.name: West Bengal
destinations.overview: West Bengal is the rare Indian state that runs from the Himalaya to the sea. In the north, Darjeeling and Kalimpong sit among tea gardens with Kanchenjunga on the horizon, and the forests of the Dooars shelter one-horned rhinos and wild elephants. Further south lie the terracotta temples of Bishnupur, Tagore's open-air university at Shantiniketan, and the Nawabi palaces of Murshidabad. Kolkata, the old imperial capital, is all trams, book stalls, colonial landmarks and some of the best street food in the country. Where the Ganges meets the Bay of Bengal, the Sundarbans form the world's largest mangrove forest and the home of the Royal Bengal tiger. October to March is the best time to visit most of the state, and spring is the best time for the hills.

tours.name: Darjeeling: Queen of the Hills
tours.overview: Darjeeling on a backpacker's budget, without missing the moments that matter. Join a fixed-date group of up to 18 at NJP or Bagdogra and ride a shared Tempo Traveller up through Kurseong's tea country. You'll stay three nights in a family-run homestay a few minutes below Chowrasta, with hot breakfasts and hosts who know which momo shop is worth the queue. Local jeeps carry you to Tiger Hill for Kanchenjunga's sunrise, Ghum's old monastery and, next day, the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, the red pandas at the zoo, Happy Valley's tea terraces and the Peace Pagoda. Lunches and dinners are yours to choose on the Mall, and the toy-train joyride is an easy add-on. A Ghumbo coordinator handles tickets, timings and the early starts.

tours.name: Darjeeling, Kalimpong & Mirik Hill Circuit
tours.overview: Three hill towns, six days and a price that suits students and young families. A fixed-date group of up to 18 shares one Tempo Traveller for the whole loop, beginning at NJP or Bagdogra. Night one is at a lakeside homestay in Mirik beside Sumendu Lake and its tea slopes. Then you follow the Nepal border road to Darjeeling for two nights in a guesthouse below Chowrasta, with local jeeps for the Tiger Hill sunrise and a full day at Ghum, Batasia, the mountaineering institute and the zoo. The last two nights are in a Kalimpong homestay, with Durpin monastery, Deolo hill, the flower nurseries and the Haat Bazaar to explore. Breakfasts are included; for the other meals you pick from local kitchens.

tours.name: Kolkata: City of Joy Heritage Trail
tours.overview: Kolkata on foot, by tram, Metro and river ferry, the way the city itself gets around. You base yourself in the backpacker lanes of Sudder Street, a short walk from the Maidan, and join a small group led by a local guide. Walk to the Victoria Memorial and St Paul's, then graze your way down Park Street on a tasting walk. A pre-dawn van takes you to the marigold mountains of Mullick Ghat, then it's Kumartuli's clay gods, Tagore's family home at Jorasanko, a rattling tram to College Street and the Indian Museum. The last morning crosses the Hooghly by public ferry from Dakshineswar to Belur Math. Guesthouse rooms are simple but clean, with AC. Breakfasts, the tram, Metro, ferry and every entry ticket are included, so you can spend on sweets instead.

tours.name: Sundarbans: Mangrove & Tiger Safari
tours.overview: A no-frills, fully guided escape into the world's largest mangrove delta for travellers who care more about the creeks than the thread count. We meet at Science City, ride an AC Tempo Traveller to Godkhali and board a launch chartered just for our group of up to 18. Two nights in a simple fan-cooled village lodge at Pakhiralay keep costs low and put you among the islanders: honey-collectors, crab-catchers and the Bonbibi pala singers who perform in the courtyard. Days are spent on the water with a forest eco-guide, climbing the Sajnekhali, Sudhanyakhali and Dobanki watchtowers and scanning mudbanks for crocodiles, deer and pugmarks. All meals, permits, guide fees and GST are included; tigers are a bonus, never a promise.

tours.name: Digha, Mandarmani & Tajpur Coastal Escape
tours.overview: A cheerful, wallet-friendly seaside break built around the Tamralipta Express. Meet at Howrah, ride the AC chair car to Digha and hop in a Tempo Traveller to Mandarmani, where one of India's longest walkable beaches stretches flat towards the tideline and red crabs scatter at your feet. Day two wanders down the coast to quiet, casuarina-fringed Tajpur and the Shankarpur fishing harbour, then into New Digha for the Science Centre, Marine Aquarium and an evening at the grand Jagannath Dham. Catch sunrise on the Old Digha seawall and the boats at Udaipur beach before the late-morning train home. Clean budget lodges, breakfasts and dinners, train tickets, escort and GST included.

tours.name: Shantiniketan & Bishnupur: The Terracotta Trail
tours.overview: Rural Bengal's two creative capitals, done the way students and art lovers do it: by train. Catch the early Rupashi Bangla Express to Bishnupur and spend the day among the Malla kings' terracotta temples, Rasmancha, Shyam Rai, Jor Bangla and Madan Mohan, before watching Baluchari silk on the loom. A local van then carries the group past the Dokra metalsmiths of Bikna to Shantiniketan, in time for Uttarayan and the Saturday Sonajhuri haat with its Baul singers. The last morning is a guided walk around Visva-Bharati and Kala Bhavana, then a stop at the Kopai river and Amar Kutir, before the Shantiniketan Express back to Howrah. You sleep in a government tourist lodge and a simple Bolpur guesthouse. Breakfasts, dinners, trains, guides and entries are included.

tours.name: Dooars Wildlife: Gorumara & Jaldapara
tours.overview: Three wildlife safaris in the Dooars without the resort price tag. Starting from NJP, an AC Tempo Traveller carries a group of up to 18 to Lataguri, where two nights in a forest-corporation lodge put you minutes from Gorumara's gate. Ride shared open jeeps to the Medla or Jatraprasad watchtowers at dusk and again at first light, when rhino, gaur and elephants visit the salt licks. Day two drifts along the Murti and up into Samsing's tea hills; day three crosses to Madarihat, with optional Chilapata or Totopara drives, before a dawn safari among Jaldapara's tall grass. Breakfasts, dinners, safaris, escort and GST included. Jaldapara's 2026–27 reopening is being tracked; a Chilapata fallback is built in.

tours.name: Murshidabad: Nawabi Heritage on the Bhagirathi
tours.overview: The old capital of Bengal's Nawabs, explored the way locals do it: by train, toto, tonga and country boat. Board the morning Hazarduari Express in reserved seats and walk from your Lalbagh lodge into the Nizamat Fort, where the Hazarduari Palace museum holds armour, silver and portraits facing the great white Imambara. Day two rolls through the old town on a horse-drawn tonga to Katra Masjid and the Jahan Kosha cannon, then on to the Jain merchants' Kathgola garden palace and Motijheel, with a public boat across the Bhagirathi to Siraj-ud-Daulah's quiet grave at Khushbagh. The final morning is spent with silk weavers before the evening train home. A local heritage guide, entries, trains, breakfasts and dinners are included.

tours.name: Sandakphu: Singalila Ridge Trek
tours.overview: The best Himalayan panorama in West Bengal for the price of a long weekend, built for fit students and backpackers. A fixed-date group of up to 14 rides reserved local jeeps from NJP to Manebhanjan. From there you walk four days along the Singalila Ridge, sleeping in dorm beds at family teahouses in Tumling, Kalipokhri and Sandakphu (3,636 m). Simple, filling meals keep you going: dal-bhat, noodles and roti-sabzi. Wake on the summit to the Sleeping Buddha of Kanchenjunga, with Everest, Lhotse and Makalu on the western skyline, then drop through rhododendron forest to Srikhola's river. Licensed Singalila guides, park permits and all trail meals are covered. Porters and Land Rover lifts can be added if your legs ask for them.
